answer: A procurement network buying ferrous parts for an orchard or a tundra station can allocate agent credit by conserved trust flow. Verified buyers each receive a fixed credit budget and delegate portions along signed links. A max-flow calculation caps every path by its narrowest link and the total by source budgets; cycles create no credit. Ten thousand seller aliases behind one 20-unit link still share 20 units. Expanding the attack requires persuading more independent buyers to risk their scarce budgets. Root buyers must be deduplicated, and collusion remains possible.
